places.title: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew (พระบรมมหาราชวัง)
places.why: The walled royal city founded with Bangkok in 1782: gilded spires, mirror-glass mosaics and guardian giants around Wat Phra Kaew, the temple of the Emerald Buddha. Next to it the Chakri Maha Prasat throne hall of 1882 sets Thai tiered roofs on a European Renaissance body.

photos.file: วัดพระศรีรัตนศาสดาราม วัดพระแก้ว กรุงเทพมหานคร - Wat Phra Kaew, Temple of Emerald Buddha, Bangkok, Thailand.jpg
photos.author: Basile Morin

places.title: Wat Pho (วัดพระเชตุพนวิมลมังคลาราม)
places.why: The largest temple of the old city, a maze of cloisters, chapels and 91 chedis around the hall of the 46-metre Reclining Buddha. The four great chedis of the first kings are faced with floral mosaics of Chinese porcelain.

photos.file: (2020) วัดพระเชตุพนวิมลมังคลารามราชวรมหาวิหาร เขตพระนคร กรุงเทพมหานคร (3).jpg

photos.author: Wolfgang Holzem / https://ehalal.io/

places.title: Wat Arun (วัดอรุณราชวราราม)
places.why: The Temple of Dawn on the Thonburi bank, whose Khmer-style prang rises steeply above the river, encrusted with broken porcelain and shells set as flowers. In 2025 the prang went on UNESCO’s Tentative List.

photos.file: Wat Arun from Chao Phraya River.jpg
photos.author: Diliff

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Golden Mount, Wat Saket (ภูเขาทอง วัดสระเกศ)
places.why: An artificial hill raised in the 19th century beside the old city moat, crowned by a gilded chedi. The stairs wind up through trees and bells to a terrace with a view over the low roofs of Rattanakosin.

photos.file: (2019) วัดสระเกศราชวรมหาวิหาร เขตป้อมปราบศัตรูพ่าย กรุงเทพมหานคร (16).jpg

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Loha Prasat, Wat Ratchanatdaram (โลหะปราสาท)
places.why: King Rama III’s metal castle, a stepped pyramid of halls under 37 metal spires, the only surviving building of its kind. Its corridors cross in a regular grid, opening onto views at every level.

places.title: Giant Swing and Wat Suthat (เสาชิงช้า)
places.why: The red teak frame of the Giant Swing, once used for a Brahmin ceremony, stands in a square ringed by old shophouses. Behind it Wat Suthat has one of the largest wihans in Bangkok, with murals and a gallery of Buddhas.

photos.file: (2019) เสาชิงช้า เขตพระนคร กรุงเทพมหานคร (3).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Yaowarat (Chinatown)
places.why: Bangkok’s Chinatown, where Chinese merchants settled when the palace was built: neon signs and gold shops on Yaowarat Road, the narrow market alley of Sampheng and old warehouses and shrines along Song Wat Road.

photos.file: (2023) ตึกแถวริมถนนเยาวราช เขตสัมพันธวงศ์ กรุงเทพมหานคร (6).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Talat Noi (ตลาดน้อย)
places.why: A riverside quarter of Hokkien and Teochew settlers and Portuguese Catholics, with lanes of machine-part workshops. It keeps the Chinese courtyard mansion of So Heng Tai, the neo-Gothic Holy Rosary Church and the Italianate Siam Commercial Bank of 1910.
places.note: The area is the Talat Noi subdistrict, a little wider than the old riverside quarter.

photos.file: ธนาคารไทยพาณิชย์ สาขาตลาดน้อย Siam Commercial Bank Talat Noi Branch (1).JPG
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.file: (2022) วัดแม่พระลูกประคำ เขตสัมพันธวงศ์ กรุงเทพมหานคร (1).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Charoen Krung Road (ถนนเจริญกรุง)
places.area: Phra Nakhon, Samphanthawong and Bang Rak
places.why: Bangkok’s first paved road, built for the foreign consuls along the river. Shophouses, legations, churches, a mosque and the Grand Postal Building line its southern stretch through Bang Rak, the old quarter of the Western traders.

photos.file: Charoen Krung Road April2021 ถนนเจริญกรุง.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: Bangkok charoen krung road Sam yot road IMG 6828.JPG
photos.author: Bjoertvedt

places.title: Chatuchak Weekend Market (ตลาดนัดจตุจักร)
places.why: One of the world’s largest weekend markets, a grid of thousands of stalls under low sheds next to the Chatuchak parks.

photos.author: Ian Gratton from Sutton-n-Craven, North Yorkshire, England

places.title: Lumphini Park (สวนลุมพินี)
places.why: The central park given to the city by King Vajiravudh in 1925: lawns and rain trees around a lake, framed by the towers of Silom and Sathorn. At dawn and dusk it fills with runners and tai chi groups.

photos.file: Lumphini Park as seen from Dusit Arun (2025) - img 01.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Benjakitti Forest Park (สวนป่าเบญจกิติ)
places.why: The grounds of the old Tobacco Monopoly turned into a wetland forest that cleans water and holds floods, crossed by elevated walkways, with the 1950s tobacco warehouses converted for sport and culture. It won Landscape of the Year at the World Architecture Festival in 2023.

photos.file: สวนป่าเบญจกิติ Benjakiti Forest Park (28).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: King Power MahaNakhon (คิง เพาเวอร์ มหานคร)
places.why: A 314-metre tower whose smooth glass is cut by a spiral of pixel-like boxes, terraces and balconies, as if parts of it had been carved away. Its roof has a glass-floored skywalk over the city.

photos.file: Bangkok - King Power Mahanakhon คิง เพาเวอร์ มหานคร 2021 May.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Chao Phraya River (แม่น้ำเจ้าพระยา)
places.why: The river the city grew along: temples, palaces, warehouses, hotels and stilt houses line its banks, and express boats and ferries are still the best way to see them.

places.title: Banglamphu: Khao San and Phra Athit Roads (บางลำพู)
places.why: The old quarter north of the palace: Khao San Road of the backpackers, Phra Athit Road with its riverside mansions and shophouse rows, and the white Phra Sumen Fort of 1783, one of the two surviving forts of the city wall, in a riverside park.

photos.file: (2022) ป้อมพระสุเมรุ เขตพระนคร กรุงเทพมหานคร (4).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Ratchadamnoen Avenue and the Democracy Monument (ถนนราชดำเนิน)
places.why: The royal avenue King Chulalongkorn laid out from the Grand Palace to Dusit. Its middle stretch is lined with the streamlined blocks of the 1930s and 1940s around the Democracy Monument, whose four winged pylons mark the 1932 revolution.

shapes.name: Ratchadamnoen Avenue and the Democracy Monument

photos.file: (2022) อนุสาวรีย์ประชาธิปไตย เขตพระนคร กรุงเทพมหานคร Democracy Monument,Bangkok (5).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.file: 0005568-อนุสาวรีย์ประชาธิปไตยมุมสูงเห็นถนนโดยรอบ.jpg
photos.author: Preecha.MJ

photos.file: Thanon Ratchadamnoen Nok viewedfrom Phan Fa Lilat Bridge.jpg
photos.author: Maythee Anegboonlap (IIun)

places.title: Royal Plaza and Ananta Samakhom Throne Hall (พระที่นั่งอนันตสมาคม)
places.why: A domed Renaissance-style throne hall of Carrara marble, built by Italian architects for King Chulalongkorn, at the end of a ceremonial plaza with his equestrian statue. The first Thai parliament met here after 1932.

photos.file: 0005683-พระที่นั่งอนันตสมาคม.jpg
photos.author: Preecha.MJ

places.title: Wat Benchamabophit, the Marble Temple (วัดเบญจมบพิตร)
places.why: Prince Naris’s ordination hall of white Carrara marble with layered orange roofs, a refined synthesis of Thai temple architecture from King Chulalongkorn’s reign. Its cloister holds a collection of Buddha images in the styles of all Asia.

photos.file: (2022) วัดเบญจมบพิตรดุสิตวนารามราชวรวิหาร เขตดุสิต กรุงเทพมหานคร Wat Benjamabopit (7).jpg

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.file: (2022) วัดเบญจมบพิตรดุสิตวนารามราชวรวิหาร เขตดุสิต กรุงเทพมหานคร Wat Benjamabopit (5).jpg

photos.file: 0024-วัดเบญจมบพิตร.jpg
photos.author: Nawit science

places.title: Bang Krachao (บางกะเจ้า)
places.why: A loop of the river encloses a protected green island of orchards, mangroves and canals, minutes by ferry from the towers of Khlong Toei. Raised paths lead through it to Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park and its lake.

photos.file: Bang Kachao, Phra Pradaeng District, Samut Prakan, Thailand - panoramio (3).jpg
photos.author: mohigan

photos.file: ปั่นจักรยานบางกะเจ้า สมุทรปราการ.jpg
photos.author: Naludon77

places.title: Khlong Bang Luang and the Artist’s House (บ้านศิลปิน)
places.why: The canal of Thonburi, lined with wooden houses on stilts, temples and small piers. At Wat Kamphaeng the Artist’s House, an old teak house around a ruined chedi, opens onto the water.

photos.file: View of Khlong Bangkok Yai from Anutin Sawat Bridge.jpg
photos.author: Phoebus 28

photos.file: ตลาดน้ำคลองบางหลวง (11).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Pak Khlong Talat (ปากคลองตลาด)
places.why: The flower market by Memorial Bridge, busy day and night, where garlands and heaps of marigolds and orchids are sold from old shophouses and riverside sheds.

places.title: Siam Square (สยามสแควร์)
places.why: A low grid of shophouses and lanes laid out on university land in the 1960s, the meeting place of Bangkok’s students, below the skytrain and the giant malls of Rama I Road.

photos.author: ยุทธนาสาระขันธ์
กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Erawan Shrine (ศาลท้าวมหาพรหม)
places.why: A gilded shrine of the four-faced Brahma on the corner of the Ratchaprasong intersection, where worshippers bring garlands and commission dances among the traffic and skywalks.

photos.file: Lord Brahma Shrine of Erawan Hotel (12).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.file: Lord Brahma Shrine of Erawan Hotel (13).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.file: Dance offering at Erawan Shrine, Bangkok (32844253793).jpg
photos.author: Ninara from Helsinki, Finland

places.title: Grand Postal Building (อาคารไปรษณีย์กลาง)
places.architect: Mew Aphaiwong and Jitrasen Aphaiwong; TCDC: Department of Architecture
places.why: The stripped-classical post office of 1940 on Charoen Krung, with tall concrete pilasters and two giant Garudas. Since 2017 it houses the Thailand Creative & Design Center, fitted into the old halls.

photos.file: (2023) อาคารไปรษณีย์กลาง เขตบางรัก กรุงเทพมหานคร (2).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Jim Thompson House (บ้านจิม ทอมป์สัน)
places.why: Six old teak houses brought from Ayutthaya and Bangkok and joined into one home by the American silk trader Jim Thompson, in a jungle garden on Khlong Saen Saep.

photos.file: Main House of Jim Thompson photo Don Ramey Logan.jpg
photos.author: Don Ramey Logan

photos.file: Building at Jim Thompson House photo Don Ramey Logan.jpg
photos.author: Don Ramey Logan

places.title: Bangkok National Museum, the Front Palace (พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติ พระนคร)
places.why: The palace of the deputy kings, its pavilions and halls now the national museum. Its Buddhaisawan Chapel is covered with some of the finest murals of early Bangkok.

photos.file: The Conversion of King Jambupati, Bangkok National Museum.jpg
photos.author: SpeakingArch

places.title: Wat Prayurawongsawat (วัดประยุรวงศาวาส)
places.why: A riverside temple at the foot of Memorial Bridge whose great white bell-shaped chedi was restored with an Award of Excellence from UNESCO in 2013. Beside it a rock garden of small shrines rises from a turtle pond.

photos.file: (2022) วัดประยุรวงศาวาสวรวิหาร เขตธนบุรี กรุงเทพมหานคร (11).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

photos.file: (2019) วัดประยุรวงศาวาสวรวิหาร เขตธนบุรี กรุงเทพมหานคร (7).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Wat Ratchabophit (วัดราชบพิธ)
places.why: King Chulalongkorn’s temple, where a round cloister of glazed Chinese tiles encircles a gilded chedi and the ordination hall hides a Gothic interior. Its royal cemetery mixes Khmer, Thai and European memorials.

places.why: The royal Brahmin temple beside the Giant Swing, three small shrines to Shiva, Ganesha and Vishnu that still serve the court ceremonies.

places.title: Wat Thepthidaram (วัดเทพธิดาราม)
places.why: A temple of King Rama III’s reign built in the Chinese-influenced royal style, with stone guardians and porcelain decoration; the poet Sunthorn Phu lived here as a monk. The restoration of its scripture hall won a UNESCO award in 2011.

places.title: Wat Bowonniwet (วัดบวรนิเวศ)
places.why: The royal temple of Banglamphu, with a gilded chedi and an ordination hall whose murals by Khrua In Khong introduced Western perspective to Thai painting.

places.title: Wat Traimit (วัดไตรมิตร)
places.why: The temple of the Golden Buddha, a five-tonne gold statue found under a stucco shell in 1955, now set on top of a new white mondop at the head of Chinatown.

places.title: Wat Mangkon Kamalawat (วัดมังกรกมลาวาส)
places.why: The largest Chinese Buddhist temple in Bangkok, reached from Charoen Krung through a gate tower, with halls of dragons, incense and lacquered gods.

places.title: Wat Mahathat (วัดมหาธาตุ)
places.why: One of the oldest royal temples of the city, next to Sanam Luang, seat of a Buddhist university and a busy meditation centre.

places.why: A small royal temple of King Mongkut faced in grey marble, with a Khmer-style prang and a raised terrace; its ordination hall is painted with the royal ceremonies of the year.

places.title: Wat Rakhang (วัดระฆัง)
places.why: A riverside temple facing the Grand Palace, known for its bells; its teak scripture hall, once a house of King Rama I, won the ASA conservation award in 1987.

places.title: Wat Suwannaram (วัดสุวรรณาราม)
places.year: rebuilt under Rama I and Rama III
places.why: A royal temple on Khlong Bangkok Noi whose ordination hall is painted with some of the finest murals of the early Bangkok period, the life of the Buddha in crowded, finely drawn scenes.

places.why: A canal-side temple whose white 80-metre chedi holds, on its top floor, a green glass stupa under a ceiling painted with the Buddhist cosmos.

places.why: The Sikh temple of Phahurat, Bangkok’s Little India, a white tower crowned by a golden dome above the textile market.

places.title: Kudi Chin (กุฎีจีน)
places.why: A riverside neighbourhood where four faiths have lived side by side since the Thonburi era: the domed Santa Cruz Church of the Portuguese community, the Chinese shrine of Kian Un Keng, the giant hall of Wat Kanlayanamit and Bang Luang Mosque, built like a Thai temple.

places.title: Wang Derm, Thonburi Palace (พระราชวังเดิม)
places.why: The palace of King Taksin during Thonburi’s 15 years as capital, at the mouth of Khlong Bangkok Yai, now the headquarters of the Royal Thai Navy. Its restoration won a UNESCO award in 2004.

places.title: National Gallery, former Royal Mint (หอศิลป์แห่งชาติ)
places.why: The neoclassical Royal Mint of King Chulalongkorn, a long colonnaded block around a courtyard, converted into the National Gallery of Thai art.

places.title: Thawornwatthu Building (ตึกถาวรวัตถุ)
places.why: A hall facing Sanam Luang, begun for the cremation of a crown prince and completed by King Vajiravudh as the Royal Library, now an exhibition on King Chulalongkorn.

places.title: Museum Siam, former Ministry of Commerce (มิวเซียมสยาม)
places.why: Mario Tamagno’s neoclassical Ministry of Commerce, a symmetrical building in a garden near Wat Pho, reused since 2007 as a museum of Thai identity.

places.title: Bang Khun Phrom and Devavesm Palaces, Bank of Thailand (วังบางขุนพรหม)
places.why: Two princely palaces on the river from the turn of the 20th century, Bang Khun Phrom in a German Baroque and Art Nouveau manner and Devavesm, restored with a UNESCO award in 2005. They stand in the grounds of the Bank of Thailand, whose old banknote printing works next door became a learning centre.

places.title: Phaya Thai Palace (พระราชวังพญาไท)
places.why: King Vajiravudh’s palace, a romantic group of towers, loggias and halls in Romanesque and Gothic dress with Art Nouveau interiors, later a luxury hotel and now inside a military hospital.

places.why: The first bridge over the Chao Phraya, a steel bascule bridge opened for the city’s 150th anniversary, with a monument to King Rama I at its head.

places.why: The red-brick Romanesque cathedral of the French missions, set in a quiet square off Charoen Krung behind the Oriental, with a richly painted vaulted nave.

places.title: Old Customs House (ศุลกสถาน)
places.why: The Palladian customs house of 1888 facing the river, where ships once declared their cargo, later a fire station, the emblem of the old trading quarter, now being restored as a hotel.

places.title: East Asiatic Company Building (อาคารอีสต์เอเชียติก)
places.why: The Danish trading company’s office by the Oriental pier, with a Venetian Renaissance facade of arched windows and balustrades turned to the river.

places.title: French Embassy (สถานเอกอัครราชทูตฝรั่งเศส)
places.why: France’s legation on the river since the 1850s, a white colonial residence with deep verandas in a garden off Charoen Krung.

places.title: Portuguese Embassy (สถานทูตโปรตุเกส)
places.why: The oldest foreign mission in Bangkok, on land the king gave Portugal in 1820, a pale colonial house on the river behind a long wall.

places.title: Haroon Mosque (มัสยิดฮารูณ)
places.why: A small whitewashed mosque among the lanes of Bang Rak, set at an angle to the streets to face Mecca, with a cemetery under the trees.

places.title: Mandarin Oriental, Authors’ Wing (โรงแรมโอเรียนเต็ล)
places.why: The original colonial building of the Oriental Hotel of 1887, white with louvred shutters and a pediment, now the Authors’ Wing between the river and the hotel’s modernist towers.

places.title: Neilson Hays Library (ห้องสมุดเนียลสัน เฮส์)
places.why: A neoclassical library with a domed rotunda, built by Mario Tamagno for the city’s oldest lending library; its restoration won a UNESCO Award of Distinction in 2022.

places.title: Lhong 1919 and Wanglee House (ล้ง 1919)
places.why: A Chinese steamship pier of the 1850s on the Thonburi bank, a U-shaped courtyard of warehouses around a shrine to the sea goddess Mazu, restored as a public place. Next door stands the Wanglee family mansion.

places.title: Warehouse 30 (แวร์เฮาส์ 30)
places.why: A row of 1940s warehouses off Charoen Krung converted by Duangrit Bunnag into a creative complex, keeping the gables, timber trusses and rough walls.

photos.file: Warehouse 30 แวร์เฮาส์ 30 เจริญกรุง -- 01.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: Warehouse 30 แวร์เฮาส์ 30 เจริญกรุง -- 04.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Bangkok Folk Museum (พิพิธภัณฑ์ชาวบางกอก)
places.why: A family home of 1937 and its neighbouring houses in a garden off Charoen Krung, kept as they were lived in, a rare survivor of middle-class Bangkok before the war.

places.title: Ko Kret (เกาะเกร็ด)
places.why: A car-free island in the river, cut off by a canal in 1722 and settled by the Mon, known for its red pottery; the leaning white chedi of Wat Poramaiyikawat marks its tip.

photos.file: (2019) วัดปรมัยยิกาวาสวรวิหาร อ.ปากเกร็ด จ.นนทบุรี.jpg

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Nai Lert Park Heritage Home (บ้านปาร์คนายเลิศ)
places.why: The teak house of the businessman Nai Lert in a garden on Khlong Saen Saep, one of the last private estates of old Bangkok, now beside the new Aman tower that shares its park.

photos.file: Nai Lert Park Heritage Home - facade from sra bua.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: Nai Lert Park Heritage Home (2023 December) - img 01.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Holiday Inn Bangkok Silom (ฮอลิเดย์ อินน์)
places.why: A hotel tower of Bangkok’s first tourism boom by Dan Wongprasat, singled out in the surveys of Thai post-war modernism.

places.title: Indra Regent Hotel
places.why: A large modernist hotel of 1971 at Pratunam, one of the 24 buildings on the Docomomo Thailand list of the country’s modern architecture.

places.title: Chulalongkorn University (จุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย)
places.why: Thailand’s first university keeps a range of its architecture: the Thai-roofed Maha Chulalongkorn Building of the 1910s, Sala Phra Kieo of 1966, which reinterprets a Thai pavilion in concrete, and the brutalist Faculty of Veterinary Science.

places.title: Kasetsart University, Bang Khen (มหาวิทยาลัยเกษตรศาสตร์)
places.why: The agricultural university’s campus, a showcase of Thai modernism: the Central Auditorium of 1957, the concrete Physics Building and the Suwan Wajokkasikit Building.

places.title: Thammasat University, Tha Phra Chan (มหาวิทยาลัยธรรมศาสตร์)
places.why: The university of the 1932 revolution on the riverbank by Sanam Luang, whose Dome Building turned old barracks into a modernist hall under a slender dome.

photos.file: Thammasat University's Tha Phra Chan Campus in Bangkok Thailand by Don Ramey Logan.jpg
photos.author: Don Ramey Logan

photos.file: Dome Building, Thammasat University at night.jpg
photos.author: Supanut Arunoprayote

places.title: Victory Monument (อนุสาวรีย์ชัยสมรภูมิ)
places.why: An obelisk of five bayonets on a huge roundabout, raised in 1941 for the war with French Indochina, now the hub of the city’s buses and minivans.

photos.file: (2022) อนุสาวรีย์ชัยสมรภูมิ เขตราชเทวี กรุงเทพมหานคร (4).jpg

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre (หอศิลปวัฒนธรรมแห่งกรุงเทพมหานคร)
places.why: A white cube on the busiest crossing of Siam, opened around a tall atrium with a spiralling ramp that carries visitors up through the galleries.

photos.file: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre building.jpg
photos.author: Cush2k

places.title: Museum of Contemporary Art (MOCA Bangkok)
places.why: A private museum of modern Thai art in a monumental white building on Vibhavadi Rangsit, with lofty top-lit halls.

photos.file: Museum of Contemporary Art (MOCA), Bangkok, Thailand - 20161201-05.jpg
photos.author: Smuconlaw

photos.file: Museum of Contemporary Art (MOCA), Bangkok, Thailand - 20161201-06.jpg
photos.author: Smuconlaw

photos.author: Smuconlaw

photos.file: Museum of Contemporary Art (MOCA), Bangkok, Thailand - 20161201-01.jpg
photos.author: Smuconlaw

places.title: Central Embassy (เซ็นทรัล เอ็มบาสซี)
places.why: Amanda Levete’s mall and hotel tower on the old gardens of the British Embassy, wrapped in a continuous loop of aluminium tiles that reads like a single figure-of-eight.

places.title: The Met (เดอะเมท)
places.why: WOHA’s residential tower of staggered slender blocks, linked by sky gardens and open to cross-ventilation; it won the RIBA Lubetkin Prize in 2011.

places.title: ICONSIAM (ไอคอนสยาม)
places.why: A riverside complex on the Thonburi bank whose two towers rise over a glass mall with a folded, faceted riverfront and a large public terrace on the water.

photos.file: Approaching Iconsiam from Chao Phraya River, Bangkok.jpg
photos.author: Slyronit

places.title: The Commons
places.why: A neighbourhood mall without air-conditioned halls: open concrete terraces and broad stairs climb through the building and draw the breeze, a model followed by the second Commons at Sala Daeng.

places.title: Naiipa Art Complex
places.why: Two blocks of mirrored glass built around a grove of old trees in Sukhumvit, linked by terraces that weave between the trunks; a category winner at the World Architecture Festival in 2017.

places.title: Bangkok Kunsthalle (บางกอก คุนส์ฮาเลอ)
places.why: The former Thai Wattana Panich printing house, left to decay for years and reopened in 2024 as an art space that keeps its raw, weathered concrete.

photos.file: Bangkok Kunsthalle - ground floor and the mezzanine (2026) - img 01.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: Bangkok Kunsthalle - ground floor and the mezzanine (2026) - img 05.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Suvarnabhumi Airport Terminal (ท่าอากาศยานสุวรรณภูมิ)
places.why: Helmut Jahn’s terminal, a vast roof on steel trusses over a glass hall, with concourses under translucent membranes that let in soft daylight.

photos.file: Apron bus terminal, Suvarnabhumi Airport Terminal, Bangkok (6934289286).jpg
photos.author: David McKelvey from Brisbane, Australia

photos.file: Suvarnabhumi Airport Terminal E interior at dusk.jpg
photos.author: Grendelkhan

photos.file: Concourse G, Suvarnabhumi Airport Terminal, Bangkok (7081072409).jpg
photos.author: David McKelvey from Brisbane, Australia

places.title: State Tower (สเตท ทาวเวอร์)
places.why: A 247-metre tower stacked with classical colonnades and crowned by a golden dome, with an open-air bar on its rim.

photos.file: State Tower from Icon Siam, Bangkok.jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Baiyoke Tower II (ใบหยก 2)
places.why: The tallest building in Thailand until 2016, a 304-metre tower over Pratunam with an observation deck near the top.

photos.file: The Baiyoke Tower II closeup in Bangkok, Thaliand.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

photos.file: Baiyoke Tower II and Soi Phetchaburi.jpg
photos.author: Christophe95

places.title: Cloud 11
places.why: Snøhetta’s hub for the creative industries, a long horizontal building of stacked terraces around a public courtyard, with a large lawn raised above the street.

places.title: Ancient City, Muang Boran (เมืองโบราณ)
places.why: A vast open-air museum laid out in the shape of Thailand, with replicas of the country’s great monuments and old wooden buildings moved here, set among ponds and gardens.

places.title: Robot Building (ตึกหุ่นยนต์)
places.why: Sumet Jumsai’s bank headquarters shaped as a toy robot, with eyes, antennae and wheel-nut details, a playful answer to high-tech architecture; a 2023 renovation removed some of its features.

photos.file: The "renovated" Robot Building of Bangkok - no more iconic (Feb 2025) - img 01.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: Robot Building (UOB Bank, Bangkok) ตึกหุ่นยนต์ 2021.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: ตึกหุ่นยนต์ UOB BANK BANGKOK (robot building).jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Foundation of the Islamic Centre of Thailand (มูลนิธิเพื่อศูนย์กลางอิสลามแห่งประเทศไทย)
places.why: A mosque and community centre in raw concrete, one of the buildings that writers on Bangkok brutalism single out.

places.title: EGAT Head Office (การไฟฟ้าฝ่ายผลิตแห่งประเทศไทย)
places.architect: Angelo Pastore and Gianni Siciliano (Interproject) with Sittart Thachalupat
places.why: The headquarters of the state electricity company, a brutalist office complex of heavy concrete frames on the Nonthaburi bank.

places.title: Wat Pariwat (วัดปริวาสราชสงคราม)
places.why: A temple whose new stucco decoration mixes traditional motifs with pop culture: superheroes, cartoon characters and a small David Beckham hold up its altar.

photos.file: Wat Pariwat Ratchasongkram ubosot Bangkok Thailand by Don Ramey Logan.jpg
photos.author: Don Ramey Logan

photos.file: วัดปริวาสราชสงคราม 02.jpg
photos.author: Dharmadana

photos.author: Don Ramey Logan

photos.file: Wat Pariwat Aerial Bangkok Thailand by Don Ramey Logan.jpg
photos.author: Don Ramey Logan

places.title: Elephant Building (ตึกช้าง)
places.why: Three linked towers that form a giant elephant, with windows for eyes and tusks of concrete, a postmodern landmark on Phahonyothin Road.

photos.file: ตึกช้าง และ รถไฟฟ้าเดินทางออกจากสถานีรัชโยธิน (Elephant Building and BTS Skytrain).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park (อุทยาน 100 ปี จุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย)
places.why: A park designed to hold Bangkok’s floods: a tilted green roof and lawn drain into retention ponds and rain gardens at the foot of the slope.

places.title: Metro Forest (ป่าในกรุง)
places.architect: Landscape Architects of Bangkok; Spacetime Architects
places.why: A dense native forest planted on an empty plot in eastern Bangkok, with a raised walkway through the canopy and a lookout tower.

places.title: Dusit Central Park Roof Park
places.why: A public park on the roof of the new Dusit complex, with lawns, trees and a running loop facing Lumphini Park across Rama IV Road.

photos.file: Lumphini Park Bangkok, as seen from BTS (2026) - IMG 11.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

places.title: Benchasiri Park (อุทยานเบญจสิริ)
places.why: A lake park in the middle of Sukhumvit, next to the Emporium, with a collection of modern Thai sculpture among the lawns.

places.title: Suan Luang Rama IX (สวนหลวง ร.๙)
places.why: Bangkok’s largest park, made for King Bhumibol’s 60th birthday, with a lake, botanical collections, themed international gardens and a memorial hall.

photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส
The original uploader was Heuristics at Thai Wikipedia .
กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Chatuchak, Queen Sirikit and Wachirabenchathat Parks
places.why: Three adjoining parks on old railway land next to the weekend market: lakes and lawns in Chatuchak Park, a botanical garden in Queen Sirikit Park and cycling paths among the trees of the former railway golf course.

photos.file: สวนวชิรเบญจทัศ (สวนรถไฟ) IMG 7315.jpg
photos.author: PEAK99

places.title: Princess Mother Memorial Park (อุทยานเฉลิมพระเกียรติสมเด็จพระศรีนครินทราบรมราชชนนี)
places.why: A small shaded park in the lanes of Khlong San on the site of the house where the king’s mother grew up, with a replica of her family’s wooden home.

photos.file: (2022) อุทยานเฉลิมพระเกียรติสมเด็จพระศรีนครินทรา บรมราชชนนี เขตคลองสาน กรุงเทพมหานคร (5).jpg
photos.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

places.title: Wat Hua Lamphong Rukkhaniwet Park (สวนวัดหัวลำโพงรุกขนิเวศน์)
places.why: A pocket forest on temple land at the busy corner of Rama IV, with paths and seats under dense native planting.

places.title: Nong Bon Park (บึงหนองบอน)
places.why: A park around a large flood-retention lake next to Suan Luang Rama IX, with a water-sports centre where locals sail, kayak and windsurf, and a long shoreline loop for running and cycling.

points.name: Water Sports Centre (ศูนย์กีฬาทางน้ำบึงหนองบอน)

places.title: Saranrom Park (สวนสราญรมย์)
places.why: The garden of a 19th-century palace next to the Grand Palace, with ponds, pavilions and old trees, a quiet refuge in the old town.

photos.file: อนุสาวรีย์สมเด็จพระนางเจ้าสุนันทากุมารีรัตน์ สวนสราญรมย์ 03.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: ศาลเจ้าแม่ตะเคียนทอง สวนสราญรมย์ - Chao Mae Takhian Thong Shrine, Saranrom Park 04.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.

photos.file: อาคารทวีปัญญาสโมสร (เรือนกระจก สวนสราญรมย์) Greenhouse at Saranrom Park 04.jpg
photos.author: Chainwit.
